marketBrief.headline: Weekend, Nov. 14: Stocks finish a winning week despite Nvidia's slide, while Bitcoin falls below $67,000 ahead of Nvidia and the Fed minutes
marketBrief.summary: US markets are closed for the weekend. The S&P 500, Nasdaq and Dow all finished the week higher, even though chip stocks fell on Friday. Bitcoin is the weak spot, quoted between about $66,500 and $67,400 depending on the source and time stamp, below its 200-week moving average, with spot ETF outflows continuing.
bullets: Friday close (AP): S&P 500 7,561.67, down 0.4% on the day but up 2.5% for the week, its first winning week since early October.
Nasdaq Composite fell 0.9% to 25,136.27 and the Dow rose 0.1% to 52,347.55. For the week, the Nasdaq gained 2.3% and the Dow 2.1% (AP).
Nvidia shares fell again Friday after Jensen Huang's resignation. Colette Kress is interim CEO; Nvidia reports fiscal Q3 on Tuesday, Nov. 17 (NVIDIA).

Saturday Bitcoin quotes vary by provider: $67,380 (Crypto Times, 3:17 a.m. UTC), $66,969 (TokenPost, 8:02 a.m. ET), $66,485 (Yahoo Finance, Saturday morning). Bitcoin is below its 200-week moving average (CoinSpectator).
The December hike is still priced after October PPI rose 0.3%, below the 0.4% forecast, with a 6.5% annual rate (BLS; CNBC). FOMC minutes are due Wednesday, Nov. 18.
